catastrophe.name: The Fracture
catastrophe.cause: Nuclear war shattered Earth into floating islands.

geography.landform: Fractured continents and floating rock islands above an atmospheric void

magnetic_fields.behavior: Erratic and turbulent in motion, but their patterns are predictable.

humanity.adaptation: Survivors evolved over generations under the influence of the magnetic fields.

objects.name: Argonaut
objects.description: Rovan’s ONE Bastion-derived Argonaut, refitted with his newfound wealth. UNIQUE silhouette: elongated rigid bronze Zeppelin central hull, two shorter side gun hulls, wedge-shaped armoured ram prow and reinforced lower keel; crimson lacquer side armour between bronze ribs, low protected command citadel, TWO exposed green magnetic stabiliser rings near the stern, FOUR articulated bronze vectoring thruster pods with green Type B glow, rebuilt gun positions. Veymarch SILVER broken shield/eight-point star on crimson banners. Workshop-built industrial machinery, not ornate fantasy gold or a generic round-nosed Bastion. HEAVY CANNON UPGRADE: two prominent twin-barrel heavy gun turrets on the upper foredeck, four huge long bronze-and-black cannon barrels, much thicker and longer than standard Bastion deck guns, with reinforced recoil cradles and visible mechanical breeches. Keep the wedge prow and crimson plating. These are conventional heavy cannons, not new magical weapons.
constraints: Exactly one Argonaut. The three captured Bastions may appear alongside it only in explicitly post-surrender fleet scenes. No wooden hulls, sails or extra vessels.
Same ship after a refit, never an additional capital ship.
All hull armour is bronze Type A; machinery is green Type B. No silver Type C hull or invulnerability.
Canonical Argonaut refit design controls hull geometry; older generic Bastion art supplies ancestry only.
Keep the wedge prow, crimson side armour, paired green stern stabiliser rings and vectoring pods recognisable in every new exterior view.
The enlarged heavy cannons must be conspicuous in exterior views; do not shrink them to decorative small deck guns.
The refit takes a legendary FOURTEEN DAYS, using captured resources; it is the same existing ship.

objects.name: New Frontier’s repainted prizes
objects.description: Josephine, Serenity and Serendipity AFTER the page20 dock repairs and quick recolouring. Three standard round-prowed Bastion capital ships, now with CRIMSON painted hull panels, bronze structural ribs and SILVER Veymarch broken-shield/star insignia. They keep their original hull shapes, standard guns and distinguishing tower/engine arrangements; do NOT become three wedge-prowed Argonaut copies or gain its huge refit cannons. Fresh paint/repair crews can be shown during the dock montage.
constraints: Exactly three prizes, plus the original Argonaut only if the shot explicitly calls for the whole fleet of FOUR.
The old fleet reference supplies hull geometry only; replace Auric gold/navy flags with crimson/silver Veymarch flags after repainting.

objects.name: Oram and its farmland
objects.description: World’s largest and richest floating city, capital of Auric Reach (earlier Oram). A vast ASYMMETRIC stratified landmass, broad agricultural shelves with patchwork fields, orchards and terraces, grain stores, dense varied urban districts, long freight gantries and a distant administrative citadel. Wealth comes from access to most farmland. Distinct geology: huge uneven multi-tiered slab with fractured cliffs and farms on lower shelves, not repeated castle-topped inverted cones. City flags GOLD with NAVY balance-in-coin. Keep a single connected metropolitan mass dominant, other fragments sparse and irregular.
constraints: Under siege, not captured. No Veymarch flags raised inside Oram.
Farmland is substantial and recognisable; do not make every fragment another identical city.

Never tile, mirror or repeat the same inverted-cone island/city silhouette. Preserve a named location’s defining geography when changing camera angle.

Trading convoys are smaller transport ships, not extra capitals. City standards remain Auric GOLD/NAVY; fleet standards Veymarch CRIMSON/SILVER. Show only ships required by the shot.
Oram is the SAME Auric Reach capital earlier called Oram, not a new duchy. Siege, not victory or surrender.
Only four owned CAPITAL ships. Smaller supply traders are a separate transport class and only appear when requested.
Maintain spatial ownership: Veymarch crimson/SILVER ships outside, Auric GOLD/NAVY city inside.
Unique broad agricultural city geography, varied low districts, irregular cliff shelves and farmland. Never tile identical conical castle islands.

All airborne vessels are rigid mechanical bronze/metal Zeppelin-like ships. ANY wooden sailing boats or cloth sails seen in an old scene reference are obsolete errors: REPLACE them with small bronze Zeppelin commuter hulls, keeping background positions.

Foreground one crimson wedge Argonaut with four huge cannon barrels, three crimson ROUND-prowed Bastion prizes with standard guns. All ship flags crimson/SILVER Veymarch. City far behind uses GOLD/NAVY Auric banners. No fifth ship in this establishing shot. Cannons begin with thin curling smoke at siege positions; do not obliterate the city or show occupation. Make this city much larger than New Frontier: monumental low horizontal urban sprawl, grain terraces and varied districts, not copied cathedral islands.

STYLE: Magneton graphic novel: painted ink, tactile bronze machinery, silver Type C, crimson Veymarch cloth, navy/gold Auric Reach uniforms; atmospheric floating islands. Consistent with supplied scene references, not photorealistic.
